access_method: REST API with API Key (parameter: demtype=COP30)
license: Open Data / Copernicus WorldDEM-30 License (Free for research and commercial use)
coverage: Mumbai Metropolitan Bounding Box: 72.65°E to 73.10°E, 18.85°N to 19.35°N
temporal_coverage: Static 2020 Release (derived from radar satellite missions 2011-2015)
authentication_requirement: OpenTopography API Key (configured in .env as OPENTOPOGRAPHY_API_KEY)
processing_steps: API subset request for Mumbai bbox -> saved as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) -> SHA-256 verified
limitations: Digital Surface Model (DSM) includes tree canopy and building heights; not a bare-earth surveyed DTM.

dataset: ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 Global 10m Land Cover
access_method: Direct GeoTIFF download from AWS S3 (arn:aws:s3:::esa-worldcover)
variables: land_cover_class (10: Tree, 50: Built-up, 60: Bare, 80: Water, 90: Herbaceous wetland, 95: Mangroves)
processing_steps: Tile extraction for N18E072 / N19E072 -> clipped to Mumbai extent -> categorized into hydraulic Manning roughness & imperviousness
limitations: Categorical raster; hydrological parameters (Manning n, Horton infiltration) are derived via empirical lookup tables.

provider: India Meteorological Department (IMD) / MCGM Disaster Management
dataset: Mumbai Urban Flood Historical Observations Archive (2016–2025)
url: Official BMC Disaster Management Cell Records / IMD Mumbai Regional Meteorological Centre
license: Government Open Data / Public Disaster Management Record
coverage: Greater Mumbai municipal area (all 24 administrative wards)
processing_steps: GeoJSON validation -> coordinate integrity check -> loaded into PostgreSQL/PostGIS table historical_flood_events
limitations: Point observations based on municipal incident logs and emergency dispatch calls; flood depth recorded at discrete field locations.

provider: India Meteorological Department (IMD) & MCGM Storm Water Drains Department
dataset: Automated Weather Station (AWS) Hourly Rainfall Records (2015–2025)
url: https://mausam.imd.gov.in / MCGM Automatic Weather Stations Network
coverage: 8 primary municipal stations: Colaba, Santacruz, Dadar, Kurla, Vikhroli, Bandra, Andheri, Borivali
processing_steps: CSV consolidation -> timestamp parsing (IST/UTC) -> station metadata join
limitations: Point measurements require spatial interpolation (IDW / Thiessen) to force 2D hydrodynamic overland grids.

provider: Open-Meteo Weather API (ECMWF IFS / DWD ICON-EU)
dataset: Open-Meteo High-Resolution Numerical Weather Prediction Forecast & Reanalysis
coverage: 9 monitoring points across Greater Mumbai: Colaba, Santacruz, Dadar, Kurla, Vikhroli, Bandra, Andheri, Borivali, Thane
temporal_coverage: Hourly observations and hourly forecasts up to 7 days ahead; historical archive from 1940
processing_steps: Asynchronous 9-point fetch -> in-memory 60s caching -> hyetograph construction for 2D flood solver
limitations: NWP model forecast/reanalysis, not direct physical telemetry from in-situ ground sensors.

dataset: INSAT-3DR / INSAT-3DS Level-2B Hydro-Estimator Method (HEM) Precipitation
access_method: Keycloak OpenID OAuth2 Authenticated REST API
license: Government of India / ISRO Data Policy
coverage: Indian Subcontinent / Western Coastal Region (including Mumbai)
authentication_requirement: MOSDAC Registered Account (configured in .env as MOSDAC_user_email and MOSDAC_pass)
processing_steps: JWT token acquisition -> APIOS granule search -> bounding box spatial clipping
limitations: Thermal infrared cloud-top temperature derivation; can overestimate rain in thick non-precipitating cirrus anvils.

provider: NASA Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center (GES DISC)
dataset: Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for GPM (IMERG)
access_method: NASA Earthdata Login / CMR OpenSearch API & HTTPS Granule Download
license: NASA Open Data Policy (Unrestricted open access)
temporal_coverage: Half-hourly (30 minutes); 2000-present for Final, real-time for Early (4h latency)
update_frequency: Every 30 minutes (Early: ~4h latency; Late: ~14h latency; Final: ~3.5 months delayed with monthly rain gauges)
authentication_requirement: NASA Earthdata Bearer Token (configured in .env as NASA_EARTHDATA_TOKEN)
download_date: 2026-09-24 (Historical 2005 deluge grid in package; live CMR search integrated)
processing_steps: CMR granule discovery -> spatial subsetting -> HDF5/NetCDF reading -> PostGIS storage
limitations: 10 km pixel footprint is coarse for micro-scale urban street inundation; best used for regional convective storm tracking.

dataset: BRIMSTOWAD Drainage Network, Holding Ponds & Pumping Stations Inventory
url: https://portal.mcgm.gov.in / BRIMSTOWAD Master Plan & GIS Layers
license: Government Open Data / Public Municipal Infrastructure Record
coverage: Greater Mumbai Stormwater Catchments (Mithi, Irla, Cleaveland, Britannia, Haji Ali)
resolution: Asset-level vector points and line channels
processing_steps: GeoJSON validation -> PostGIS database import into pumping_stations, drainage_nodes, drainage_links
limitations: Static rated engineering capacity; real-time SCADA pump discharge and water level telemetry are not exposed via public APIs.

provider: Survey of India (SOI) / Mumbai Port Trust / INCOIS
dataset: Apollo Bunder (Mumbai) Hourly Tide Observations & Astronomical Benchmarks
url: https://incois.gov.in & Survey of India Tide Tables
access_method: CSV archive and tidal benchmark schema
temporal_coverage: Historical 2005 deluge series (July 25–27, 2005) & Annual MHWS/HAT benchmarks
update_frequency: Tidal constituents static; operational tide predicted
processing_steps: Chart datum to MSL offset calibration (MSL = CD - 2.51m) -> downstream boundary input for coastal outfall locking
limitations: Historical series for 2005 event; real-time operational storm surge requires live INCOIS coastal telemetry.

url: https://dm.mcgm.gov.in / Disaster Management Cell Shelter Directory
coverage: 10 major designated municipal schools and relief centres across Mumbai wards
processing_steps: GeoJSON validation -> loaded into PostGIS table shelters -> linked to simulation impact analysis
limitations: 10 primary designated shelters documented; temporary emergency shelters during severe mass evacuations are mobilized dynamically.
